# Skein 0.6.1 — full agent context

Skein is a small HTML-first runtime for native Web Components. Treat DOM, Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, CSS, SVG, Canvas, Web Audio and browser APIs as primary. Skein adds fine-grained reactive state, compiled path bindings, keyed DOM identity and scoped lifecycle.

## Component files

`<user-card>` maps to `user/card.html`; hyphens become path separators and `.html` is appended. A component file may contain top-level `<script>`, markup and `<style>`.

Inline demos may use `<template skein="tag-name">` plus the same component source.

Unknown custom tags are not eagerly claimed. Skein first fetches the matching HTML source; only a successful load causes `customElements.define`. A 404 leaves the tag undefined for another library.

`Skein.define(tag, source)` is explicit registration for tooling/generated source and defines once. Production hot-reload instance/reload/generation machinery does not exist.

## Reactive state

Inside a component script, `this` is Proxy-backed reactive state.

Only arrays and plain/null-prototype objects are recursively reactive. Date, Map, Set, DOM nodes, AudioContext and class instances remain native/opaque. Their internal mutations are not automatically observable.

Reactive raw→proxy, proxy→raw and dependency registries are module-global WeakMaps. Passing the same raw plain object between components preserves one Skein Proxy identity rather than creating proxy-of-proxy state.

Reads track raw-object/property dependency nodes. Missing own property reads track too. Prototype properties never leak through binding lookup. Object enumeration has a structural dependency. Array structural changes notify required length/index dependencies. Failed Reflect writes/deletes do not notify.

## Paths and bindings

Bindings are strict dotted property paths, not JavaScript expressions. Examples: `count`, `user.name`, `$index`. Invalid whitespace/empty segments/expressions fail during compilation.

```html
<h1>{user.name}</h1>
<div title="User {user.name}" data-id={id}></div>
<label for={inputId}>Name</label>
<input .value={name}>
<button ?disabled={saving}>Save</button>
<button @click={save}>Save</button>
<reactor-core --load={reactor.load}></reactor-core>
```

Meaning:
- unprefixed dynamic attribute → string/native attribute;
- `.name={path}` → DOM property;
- `?name={path}` → boolean attribute;
- `@event={path}` → event listener.
- `--name={path}` → one CSS custom property through `element.style`.

Special bindings require exactly one path. `<style>` contents are opaque to Skein parsing.

CSS custom-property bindings are fine-grained CSSOM writes. Any value other than `null`, `undefined` or `false` calls `element.style.setProperty('--name', value)` for that property only. Those three removal values call `element.style.removeProperty('--name')`; `0` is retained. Skein does not construct or assign a serialized `style` string. Ordinary static inline declarations and unrelated custom properties on the same element remain untouched. If a static `style` declares the same custom property, the binding targets that declaration and a removal value removes it from the inline style. Do not combine per-property bindings with a reactive whole-`style={path}` binding on the same element because those writes have competing ownership.

```html
<reactor-core
  style="display:block; contain:layout"
  --temperature={reactor.temperature}
  --load={reactor.load}>
</reactor-core>
```

CSS custom properties set on a custom-element host inherit through its Shadow DOM normally, so internal styles can consume `var(--temperature)` and `var(--load)` without a framework-specific input or string style binding.

`in={...}` does not exist. Use explicit full paths outside list item scopes.

## Lists

```html
<li each={items} key={id}>
  {index}: {title}
</li>
```

`each` creates item scopes. Locals are `index`, `$index` and `$value`; lookup falls outward through list scopes to root.

Explicit keys are preflighted before reconciliation mutates views. Null/undefined or duplicate keys throw. Existing records keep DOM/view identity, removed records dispose, and surviving ranges move with native `moveBefore()` when available or `insertBefore()` fallback.

Without explicit keys, object items use identity and primitive values use value+occurrence identity. Prefer stable explicit keys for records.

## Conditions

```html
<section if={visible}>...</section>
```

A branch owns a child Scope and current View. Hide permanently disposes the view and removes its nodes; show creates a fresh view.

## Composition model

Use three browser mechanisms:

```text
data      → DOM properties
/actions/ ← bubbling + composed CustomEvent
content   → native <slot>
```

There is no Skein event bus, provide/inject system, framework store or framework slot abstraction.

### Inputs

Child declaration:

```js
input('name', 'Metric')
input('value', 0)
```

Static primitive configuration may be written as literal attributes:

```html
<ui-metric name="Active" tone="lime"></ui-metric>
```

Live values and all objects/functions use DOM properties:

```html
<ui-metric name="Active" .value={active}></ui-metric>
<task-card .task={task}></task-card>
```

`input(name, fallback)` initialization precedence:

```text
pre-mount own DOM property > same-name static attribute > fallback
```

Attribute conversion is inferred from fallback type:
- boolean fallback: presence means true;
- number fallback: `Number(attribute)`, NaN throws;
- object/function fallback: attribute is rejected; require a property;
- string/undefined/null fallback: attribute text remains string.

After initialization, the host property accessor is backed by child reactive state. Direct later property assignment is reactive. A static attribute is **only an initial seed**; changing it after mount does not update state. Do not describe attributes as a second reactive input channel.

Input names that collide with `state` or inherited Skein/HTMLElement host APIs such as `title`/`dispose` throw.

### Outputs

Child-to-owner communication is native DOM events:

```js
host.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('task-select', {
  detail: { id: this.task.id },
  bubbles: true,
  composed: true
}))
```

A bubbling + composed event may cross several nested Shadow DOM boundaries directly. Do not write relay handlers in intermediate components unless they intentionally transform domain semantics.

### Content / layout

Skein components use real Shadow DOM. Use native default/named slots:

```html
<!-- ui/panel.html -->
<header><slot name="heading"></slot></header>
<slot></slot>
```

```html
<ui-panel>
  <span slot="heading">Tasks</span>
  <task-board .tasks={tasks}></task-board>
</ui-panel>
```

`slotchange` and `assignedElements()` remain browser APIs.

## Application-scale reference

`examples/workspace/` is the composition proof. It contains 18 component types:

```text
workspace-app
└─ workspace-shell
   ├─ workspace-sidebar
   ├─ workspace-topbar
   ├─ workspace-overview
   │  ├─ workspace-metrics → ui-metric
   │  ├─ ui-panel → project-list → project-row
   │  ├─ ui-panel → task-board → task-column → task-card
   │  ├─ ui-panel → team-strip → ui-avatar
   │  └─ ui-panel → activity-feed → activity-item
   └─ detail-drawer
```

It intentionally has no framework communication primitive beyond inputs plus browser events/slots. Root state flows down through properties; leaf actions bubble through several shadow roots without relays; shell/panel layout uses named/default slots.

`test/workspace.mjs` runs the generated production runtime in Chromium and verifies all 18 definitions, native slot assignment, primitive static inputs, pre-mount property precedence, search reactivity, deep composed-event propagation, task mutation and conditional teardown.

The scale test exposed the static primitive input attribute gap; that is why 0.6.1 adds attribute seeding. It did not justify a store, router, bus, provide/inject API or framework slots.

## Scheduler / computed / effects

`computed(fn)` returns lazy cached derived state. `effect(fn)` creates a user effect.

Synchronous writes enqueue one microtask. Scheduler behavior is render effects to exhaustion → one user effect → render effects again if dirtied → next user effect. User effects therefore observe settled DOM.

There is no public `batch()`.

## Scope and lifecycle

Scope owns child scopes, effects/computed refs, cleanup callbacks and a lazily allocated AbortController.

`onCleanup(fn)` registers permanent cleanup. `abortSignal` exposes the scope signal for native listener/fetch APIs.

Custom Element lifecycle:
- connect mounts once or resumes paused view;
- disconnect pauses;
- reconnect resumes dirty work without rebuilding DOM;
- `connectedMoveCallback` preserves state during supported platform moves;
- `host.dispose()` is permanent teardown.

Mount is transactional: failed template instantiation disposes the fresh Scope and clears partial shadow DOM before reporting the error.

Dynamic view teardown force-disposes only nested SkeinElement instances. Third-party custom elements rely on normal disconnected lifecycle; Skein never calls arbitrary external `dispose()` methods.

## Native resources

Prefer ordinary local variables for imperative browser resources such as AudioContext or CanvasRenderingContext. They may be stored in state, but Skein returns them unchanged and does not observe internal mutation. Feed continuous visual state into native CSS with individual `--name={path}` bindings rather than rebuilding a whole `style` attribute.

## Public surface

```js
Skein.version
Skein.define(tag, source)
```

Injected component names:

```text
input
computed
effect
onCleanup
host
abortSignal
```

Do not invent `Skein.stats`, `Skein.flush`, `Skein.Signal`, `signal()`, `batch()`, `untrack()`, JSX expressions, framework slots, SSR/hydration/suspense/error-boundary claims.

## Production build

`tools/build.mjs` concatenates readable modules and lexically minifies/mangles known internals with zero dependencies. It is not an AST transform; native/public property names must not be carelessly added to its mangle map.

Current 0.6.1 artifact: 15,839 B raw / 5,686 B gzip / 5,123 B Brotli.

Run:

```bash
node tools/build.mjs
node tools/build.mjs --check
node test/run.mjs
node test/workspace.mjs
```

The main Chrome suite covers readable/generated runtime, fine-grained CSS custom-property set/remove behavior, ordinary inline-style and Shadow DOM interaction, keyed identity, invalid keys, mount rollback, native dynamic `for`, third-party Custom Element coexistence, input timing/collisions, shared Proxy identity, native objects, lifecycle, late define and Studio. The Workspace suite is the application-scale production composition regression.

## 0.6 migration

```diff
- <li for={items} key={id}>...</li>
+ <li each={items} key={id}>...</li>

- <address in={user.address}>{city}</address>
+ <address>{user.address.city}</address>

- this.value = input('value', .5)
+ input('value', .5)
```

The old input assignment form remains compatible. Skein 0.6.1 adds primitive literal-attribute seeding for matching `input()` declarations and fine-grained `--name={path}` CSS custom-property bindings.
